concept.title: Cross references
concept.abstract: This section covers Cross-References, Bookmarks and Hyperlinks — three distinct navigational mechanisms that connect related content within a document, across a documentation set, or to an external resource — and six scenarios: an internal cross-reference or bookmark, an external URL, a hyperlink with non-descriptive display text, a link list at the end of a section, and an internal link list used as a mini-TOC. The converter maps each structured link to a DITA <xref> element using @href, @scope, and @format to resolve the target correctly in the generated output.

conbody.p: A cross-reference, a bookmark, and a hyperlink are three distinct mechanisms - each with a specific structural role:

ul.li: A cross-reference is an active, field-based link to a heading, figure, table, footnote, or bookmark within the same document or internal identifier (such as bookmark).

A bookmark assigns a named identifier to a specific location in the document — a word, a phrase, a paragraph, or a position between characters. Bookmarks serve as anchor points that cross-references and hyperlinks can target.Both cross-reference and/or bookmarks target updates automatically when the document is restructured or the sections are moved within the same document.

A hyperlink stores an explicit address — a URL, an email address, a file path, or a sometimes same-document bookmark anchor. Unlike bookmark and cross reference, the hyperlink address is fixed at the time of creation. Using the document's native link tools is the condition that produces a valid, resolvable element in the DITA output. A link typed as plain text produces no link structure and maps to a plain

element. In Markdown, hyperlinks are created using standard link syntax, where the link text identifies the visible label and the target specifies the destination. For example:[Alarm Notifier](alarm-notifier.md)

conbody.p: The converter analyzes each link target to determine whether it references an internal Markdown topic, an external website, or a collection of related topics. Internal Markdown links are converted into DITA <xref> elements that reference the corresponding generated DITA topics. External URLs are converted into DITA cross references with the appropriate scope and format attributes. When a collection of links represents related topics rather than the primary content of a topic, the converter generates a DITA <related-links> section containing structured <link> elements.Use meaningful link text and valid link targets so that related information can be resolved correctly during conversion. Place links to related topics in a dedicated Related Topics section. When a section contains only links to related Markdown topics, the converter can generate a structured DITA <related-links>section.
The following scenarios demonstrate how different Markdown cross-reference patterns are interpreted during Markdown-to-DITA conversion and how they affect the generated DITA output.
